prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1200; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a side impact collision at a signalized intersection involving the insured vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant reports a back strain and is represented by counsel, who has asked that all communication be routed through their office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which records the collision as described and places the claimant in the vehicle at the time. The responding officer noted the points of impact on both vehicles.

Entry 3: Obtained statements from two independent witnesses and the other driver. Each account matches the claimant's description of how the crash happened, including the direction of travel and the signal phase.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who confirmed representation and provided a medical authorization. The claimant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation so far.

Entry 5: Inspected the insured vehicle and reviewed scene photographs. The damage to the driver's side and door panel lines up well with the impact described, and no older damage has been identified.

Entry 6: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 7: Reviewed the claimant's medical records. The reported back strain fits the kind and force of a side impact of this type. No prior injury to the same area appears in the records or in the claimant's history.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course, beginning with urgent care, then physical therapy. Visits have tapered as the claimant's symptoms improved, and the provider's notes reflect steady progress.

Entry 9: Requested updated treatment notes from the provider to confirm current status. Reviewed the file with the counsel's office to make sure all requested documents are in hand.

Entry 10: Compared the vehicle repair estimate against the inspection findings. The line items correspond to the damage areas documented at the scene, and no unrelated repairs are included.

Entry 11: Based on the current file, the claim is moving forward on the normal timeline. Next step is to review the updated treatment notes once received and finalize the evaluation with counsel.
